coverage: All 55 pasted entries, deduplicated to 48 works. No original recommendation thread was supplied; linked rating pages are evidence, not candidate sources.

books.title: The Path Between the Seas
books.author: David McCullough
books.eligibility: Multinational construction history for general readers; the engineering is explained within a narrative.
books.theme: 0: The core is a multinational infrastructure project and world trade; disease and local politics are supporting constraints.
reason: Documentary reporting and an established historical method support E18/A5. This is a reconstructed project history, not a controlled comparison of canal projects.

Engineering limits, finance, labor, health logistics and diplomacy form linked constraints, supporting M15/U13/S12/F7. The reusable lesson concerns project organization under interacting bottlenecks, not canal trivia.
The long narrative earns much of its space, but personal and diplomatic detail keeps D7. The underlying infrastructure lessons support R9.
The chronology accumulates clearly and the prose is controlled, supporting N3/P2. The fresh nomination supplies no evidence for increasing any component.

books.title: The Power Broker
books.author: Robert A. Caro
books.eligibility: Investigative political biography and urban history; it does not teach a specialist procedure.
books.theme: -10: American urban and political history predominates.
reason: Extensive documentary and interview research supports E18/A5. A powerful account of one administrator's rise is still a case study, not proof that every institution operates identically.
Public authorities, debt, patronage and infrastructure control support M15/U13/S10/F6. These mechanisms survive removal of local personalities, so V3 does not apply.
The very long local and biographical account costs D5; the institutional lessons retain R9.
Caro's cumulative structure and precise narrative retain N3/P2. The pasted 93 and 94 are neither evidence nor a basis for averaging; the full prior vector remains justified.

books.title: Why We Fight
books.author: Christopher Blattman
books.eligibility: An explanatory argument about bargaining and violence, with cases across several scales; policy advice is incidental.
books.theme: 0: Comparative conflict mechanisms across countries and organizations; no listed theme predominates.
reason: Blattman's research background and explicit bargaining framework support E17/A5. The five-part classification organizes evidence but is not itself a causal test of each conflict.

Unchecked interests, intangible incentives, uncertainty, commitment problems and misperception support M16/U14/S11/F6. They transfer from interstate conflict to smaller organizations, with limits on prediction.
The synthesis is fairly concentrated, D8, and the core bargaining problems should outlast current conflicts, R8.
Examples make the argument cumulative and readable, N3/P2. Its useful general mechanisms establish a payload without accepting a claim to explain every war completely.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.author: Adam Higginbotham
books.eligibility: Investigative history of a reactor failure and its institutions, not a reactor-engineering manual.
books.theme: 0: Reactor failure and information control are central; environmental damage and illness are consequences, not the main explanatory subject.
reason: Archival work and eyewitness reconstruction support E18/A4. Technical and institutional explanations merit serious credit, while reconstructed dialogue and inaccessible records still warrant moderate confidence.
Reactor behavior, operating constraints, authority and suppressed information support M16/U13/S11/F7. The main transfer is failure analysis in tightly coupled organizations.
The narrative mostly advances the causal account, D8; design and organizational failure modes remain durable, R9.
Clear sequencing and controlled explanation support N3/P2. Rechecking the scope does not establish a serious veto or a predominant environmental theme; the previous vector stays intact.

books.title: Challenger
books.author: Adam Higginbotham
books.eligibility: Archival narrative of the shuttle program and disaster, not astronaut or engineering training.
books.theme: -10: The American technological-disaster narrative predominates. Strong engineering fit does not waive the American-tragedy rule.
reason: Archival reporting and documentary reconstruction support E18/A4. Public critical reception supports the reporting and presentation, not automatic maximum points.
Hardware limits, escalation of commitment, launch pressure and information flow support M16/U14/S11/F7. The account has clear value for engineering and institutional risk.
Extended astronaut and program biographies reduce D to 6. The failure mechanisms justify R9 despite the recent publication.
The causal chronology remains clear and memorable, N3/P2. The US disaster focus retains the thematic deduction; the supplied 93 cannot be a total under that deduction.

books.title: Lords of Finance
books.author: Liaquat Ahamed
books.eligibility: International monetary history told through four central bankers, not a finance textbook.
books.theme: 0: The international monetary system and cross-border transmission are central.
reason: Ahamed's financial expertise and historical synthesis support E17/A5. Organizing the Depression around four bankers risks giving personalities more causal weight than the entire system warrants.
Gold-standard constraints, international debts and policy coordination support M14/U13/S12/F6. The book links policy choices across economies, but offers less mechanism than a full monetary history.
Biographical material lowers D to 7; the historical monetary constraints retain R9.
The four-person structure is readable and the prose disciplined, N3/P2. This limitation reduces points rather than establishing a central epistemic failure.

books.title: When Genius Failed
books.author: Roger Lowenstein
books.eligibility: Reported financial history of LTCM, not trading instruction or a quantitative-finance reference.
books.theme: 0: A globally connected financial failure and reusable risk mechanisms; an American fund's address alone is insufficient.
reason: Reported access and a coherent reconstruction support E17/A4. The narrative cannot independently audit every position or estimate in a private fund.
Leverage, funding liquidity, crowded trades and forced liquidation support M16/U14/S11/F7. The lesson is about model assumptions and balance-sheet constraints, not a rejection of mathematics.
The compact case history earns D8, and the feedback mechanisms retain R9 across market regimes.
The rise-and-failure structure is clear and economical, N3/P2. No serious veto is established; the book is historical explanation rather than investment instruction.

books.title: Chokepoints
books.author: Edward Fishman
books.eligibility: A narrative and explanatory account of economic coercion, not sanctions-compliance instruction.
books.theme: 0: Cross-border finance, technology and geopolitical coercion are central; US policy has international influence throughout.
reason: Fishman's policy experience and interviews support E17/A4. Insider access is valuable but does not neutralize the perspective of the institutions imposing sanctions.
Financial networks, technology access and jurisdiction support M15/U14/S12/F7. Network position can create coercive power; outcomes also depend on adaptation and coalition support.
The policy narrative is substantial but sometimes person-centered, D7. Specific instruments and political conditions change, so R7.
The book offers a coherent account with clear distinctions, N3/P2. A current subject alone is not V4: durable mechanisms remain after individual disputes pass.

books.title: Upstart: How China Became a Great Power
books.author: Oriana Skylar Mastro
books.eligibility: A sustained argument organized by strategic emulation, exploitation and entrepreneurship across three policy domains; not a technical monograph or training text.
books.theme: 0: Thematic analysis of international strategy, not predominantly a chronological national history. This corrects the earlier -10.
reason: Mastro's research expertise supports A5; reconstructing state strategy from selected behavior limits E to 16. Strategic intent and success should not be inferred from outcomes alone.
Emulation, exploitation and entrepreneurship connect diplomatic, military and economic policy, supporting M15/U14/S12/F7. These categories are useful competing explanations, not guaranteed forecasts.
The focused argument supports D8, while ongoing strategic competition and less-tested claims limit R to 7.
The thematic structure earns N2/P2. All ten positive components remain supported. The contents now give a better basis for classifying the book as strategic explanation, so T changes from -10 to 0.
books.editionNote: Hardback selected: the official Oxford preview identifies 9780197695067 as hardback. No official paperback edition was verified; third-party paperback labeling of that same ISBN was rejected.

books.sourceTitle: The Rise and Fall of the Great Powers
books.title: The Rise and Fall of the Great Powers
books.author: Paul Kennedy
books.eligibility: Comparative world history linking productive resources to military power; not a specialist reference.
books.theme: 0: Comparative relations among multiple great powers.
reason: Kennedy's scholarship supports E17/A5. Broad historical comparisons cannot isolate productive capacity from every political, military and institutional cause.
Resource mobilization, relative economic weight and commitments support M15/U13/S12/F7. These are strategic constraints, not a mechanical law that wealth determines victory.
Large scope and extensive case detail reduce D to 6. Historical mechanisms retain R9; late-twentieth-century projections must be read as dated forecasts.
The organizing argument remains readable and controlled, N3/P2. Obsolete predictions are not being represented as current information, so they do not establish V1 here.

books.title: Apple in China
books.author: Patrick McGee
books.eligibility: Investigative corporate and industrial history, not a manufacturing or supply-chain manual.
books.theme: 0: Transnational production and technology transfer dominate; this is not a general national history of China.
reason: Reporting on an opaque company and supplier network supports E16/A4. Interviews and corporate figures do not by themselves prove how much of China's industrial rise Apple caused.
Supplier capability, process knowledge, scale and geopolitical dependence support M16/U14/S12/F7. These are unusually useful industrial mechanisms.
Corporate detail lowers D to 7; a recent interpretation of an evolving relationship keeps R7.
The industrial narrative is coherent and readable, N3/P2. Current reviews add support but not an independent causal experiment; the prior 88 remains justified.

books.title: The House of Morgan
books.author: Ron Chernow
books.eligibility: An archival history of an international banking network, not a banking textbook.
books.theme: 0: An international banking network across London, New York, Europe and state finance; not predominantly domestic American issues.
reason: Archives, interviews and long historical reach support E18/A5. The family-and-firm focus is strong documentary history but can foreground elite decisions.
Credit relationships, reputation, capital mobilization and state finance support M14/U13/S12/F6. The international network gives more than domestic biographical interest.
The large volume of personalities and chronology lowers D to 5. Financial intermediation and institutional trust retain R9.
The narrative joins its generations and institutions clearly, N3/P2. No serious veto is established, and international influence is central rather than incidental.

books.sourceTitle: The Death and Life of Great American Cities
books.title: The Death and Life of Great American Cities
books.author: Jane Jacobs
books.eligibility: A sustained argument about how cities work. Its recommendations do not make its main structure an urban-planning manual.
books.theme: -10: Urban history and urban organization predominate.
reason: Comparative observation and a lasting contribution to urban thought support E16/A5. The argument is not a controlled test of each proposed neighborhood mechanism.
Mixed use, informal surveillance, diversity and local feedback support M15/U13/S11/F5. They transfer to complex-system design, but much of the practical content stays urban.
Some repeated examples and local detail keep D7; the core coordination questions retain R9.
The argument is cumulative, memorable and carefully expressed, N3/P2. It remains explanatory rather than a procedural design manual. The same urban deduction and prior total remain justified.

books.title: Cadillac Desert
books.author: Marc Reisner
books.eligibility: Investigative environmental and water-policy history, not hydraulic-engineering instruction.
books.theme: -10: Environmental issues and American regional history predominate; one deduction only.
reason: Investigative evidence supports E16/A4. Polemical framing and historical data require care; old water figures are not being treated as current.
Subsidies, allocation rules, engineering commitments and institutional incentives support M14/U12/S11/F5. There is a transferable account of distorted infrastructure decisions.
The lengthy regional history lowers D6. Its institutional lessons retain R8, with less durability for specific conditions and figures.
The narrative is clear and forceful, N3/P2. Environmental focus makes it a low reading priority for this user, but that focus is not a veto. The earlier 71 remains supported.

books.title: Merchants of Grain
books.author: Dan Morgan
books.eligibility: A narrative account of commodity-trading firms and institutions, not a trading manual.
books.theme: 0: International commodity trade, finance and state bargaining.
reason: Morgan's reporting and access support E17/A4. The source's author-list link must not confuse the journalist with a different writer of the same name.
Information advantages, storage, freight, finance and state bargaining support M15/U14/S12/F7. Commodity intermediation is close to the requested domain.
The focus on trading institutions earns D8. R8 recognizes durable mechanisms while discounting a decades-old map of firms and markets.
The connected business narrative supports N3/P2. This reassessment retains the prior vector; neither repeated nomination nor the pasted higher reader average establishes new quality.

books.title: The Anarchy
books.author: William Dalrymple
books.eligibility: Popular historical narrative of the East India Company's conquest, not a specialist technical monograph.
books.theme: -10: The dominant narrative is conquest and rule in India. Corporate and cross-border mechanisms do not erase that regional historical focus.
reason: Historical research and broad readership support E17/A4. A narrative of conquest does not isolate each cause as a comparative economic study would.
Corporate finance, military contracting, alliances and delegated sovereignty support M14/U12/S11/F6. These mechanisms prevent V3, but analogy with present corporations needs restraint.
Battle and court detail lower D7. The historical account remains useful independently of current corporate controversies, R9.
Strong chronology and readable prose support N3/P2. The dominant India-centered historical narrative receives T=-10 despite international capital and British political links.

books.title: How Africa Works
books.author: Joe Studwell
books.eligibility: A comparative development argument supported by historical cases and reporting; it is not an economics course or investment manual.
books.theme: 0: Comparative economic development across African states; demography and agriculture are mechanisms, not predominantly disease or ecological advocacy.
reason: Reporting and comparative history support some evidential credit, E14/A4. The author-published exchange with Hafez Ghanem exposes a live dispute over manufacturing-led growth and the interpretation of Ethiopia.

Population density, public-goods costs, agricultural productivity and industrial learning support M14/U13/S11/F6. They are plausible mechanisms; selecting successful cases does not establish that the full policy package transfers.
Case detail and thesis repetition keep D7. The mechanisms have potential durability, but the optimistic forward case warrants R7 and low score confidence.
The account is accessible and organized, N3/P2. Newness alone is not hype dependence, and the checked criticism does not establish a serious central failure; retain it provisionally.
books.editionNote: Hardback selected. Profile lists hardback 9781788167994 for 29 January 2026 and paperback 9781788168007 for 21 January 2027; the latter is future-dated as of this assessment.

books.title: The Great Bridge
books.author: David McCullough
books.eligibility: Popular history of a bridge project and its setting, not a civil-engineering textbook.
books.theme: -10: New York urban and civic history is a major organizing frame.
reason: Documentary history and McCullough's historical craft support E18/A5. It is a well-supported project case rather than a general theory tested across bridges.
Engineering constraints, project finance and organization support M14/U12/S11/F6. These make it more than a collection of local facts.
Family and New York civic history lower D6. Infrastructure and project lessons remain durable, R9.
The narrative builds clearly and the prose is controlled, N3/P2. The urban-history deduction still applies. The fresh list does not justify changing the previous 76.

books.title: Nature’s Metropolis
books.author: William Cronon
books.eligibility: A sustained history linking a city to its hinterland. Scholarly research does not make its narrative a specialist technical reference.
books.theme: -10: Environmental and American urban history predominate; one deduction only.
reason: Extensive historical scholarship supports E18/A5. The synthesis interprets linked processes rather than estimating a single clean causal effect.
Commodity grading, transport, credit and the city-hinterland relationship support M16/U14/S12/F6. Its systems account retains substantial transferable value.
Rich local and environmental detail lowers D7; the historical mechanisms retain R9.
The large argument is unusually coherent and readable, N3/P2. Its explicit undesired-profile status and environmental/urban focus make it a low reading priority, not a fiction exclusion or V3 veto.

books.title: The Visible Hand
books.author: Alfred D. Chandler Jr.
books.eligibility: An explanatory history of firms and management. The chronological sector accounts and broad argument govern classification; its academic use does not make it a management textbook.
books.theme: -10: The rise of modern business in one national economy is the organizing history, despite international applicability.
reason: The documentary record and Chandler's standing support E16/A5. The NBER critique gives a concrete reason to withhold more evidence points: observed corporate dominance does not by itself establish superior efficiency over alternative explanations.
Throughput, coordination and organizational scale support M15/U14/S11/F7. These remain useful mechanisms without treating the rise of integrated firms as an inevitable or universally optimal outcome.
Long sector histories lower D6. The organizational questions retain R9, although the book cannot serve as a current map of firms.

The architecture is systematic but dense, N2/P2. The critique establishes causal underdetermination, not a decisive refutation of the coordination mechanism. A serious V1 failure is therefore not established, at moderate confidence.

books.title: The Cigarette Century
books.author: Allan M. Brandt
books.eligibility: Historical investigation of tobacco, science, law and business, not clinical or public-health instruction.
books.theme: -10: Tobacco-related disease and predominantly American public-health and political history.
reason: Historical investigation and Brandt's scholarship support E18/A5. The case connects evidence production with institutions rather than giving medical instructions.
Advertising, organized doubt, liability and regulation support M14/U12/S11/F4. Those mechanisms transfer, but the main subject remains tobacco and public health.
Extensive scientific, legal and cultural history lowers D6. The incentives and historical record retain R9.
The account is readable and cumulative, N3/P2. Disease and American public-health history require the deduction; its reputation cannot convert this into a top personal recommendation.

books.title: Command and Control
books.author: Eric Schlosser
books.eligibility: Investigative narrative of nuclear accidents and institutional control, not a weapon-operation or design manual.
books.theme: -10: The US nuclear-accident and disaster narrative, centered on the Damascus accident, invokes the American-tragedy theme despite global strategic relevance.
reason: Documentary investigation and specialist reporting support E18/A4. A record of accidents and near misses does not by itself produce a reliable numerical probability of nuclear catastrophe.
Safety-versus-readiness tradeoffs, information flow and organizational failure support M16/U14/S12/F7. These are strong strategic-risk mechanisms.
The long accident narrative and institutional detail keep D7. The control problems retain R9.
Clear narrative assembly and controlled reporting support N3/P2. The Damascus disaster frame triggers T=-10; this prevents the pasted 96 from surviving unchanged.

books.title: The Dead Hand
books.author: David E. Hoffman
books.eligibility: Cold War investigative history of weapons programs and diplomacy, not a weapons reference.
books.theme: 0: International arms competition, verification and weapons control; biological weapons are treated as a security problem, not predominantly as disease history.
reason: Investigative sources and reporting access support E18/A4. Secrecy leaves some uncertainty about intentions and program details.
Arms competition, command systems, verification and institutional concealment support M15/U13/S12/F7. The combination of military technology and diplomacy is a close fit.
Extensive political narrative keeps D7; the strategic mechanisms retain R8, with caution about extrapolating the historical account into current arsenals.
The sequence is clear and the prose disciplined, N3/P2. Biological weapons are part of an international security history, so their presence alone does not trigger the disease deduction.

books.title: Toms River
books.author: Dan Fagin
books.eligibility: Narrative investigation of pollution and causal evidence, not an epidemiology textbook.
books.theme: -10: Environmental contamination, disease and an American local tragedy; one deduction only.
reason: Investigative science reporting supports E18/A4. Fagin's treatment of causal uncertainty is relevant evidence against casually labeling the book an epistemic failure.
Exposure tracing, statistical inference, corporate incentives and regulatory response support M14/U12/S10/F4. Some useful reasoning survives the local setting.
The long town and legal history lowers D6. The evidence problems retain R8.
The investigation is readable and carefully structured, N3/P2. Environmental damage, disease and American local tragedy receive one deduction. It remains eligible but a low personal priority.

books.title: American Genesis
books.author: Thomas P. Hughes
books.eligibility: A broad history of technological systems and American culture, not instruction in engineering methods.
books.theme: -10: One nation's technological and cultural history is the main organizing subject.
reason: Hughes's scholarship and historical synthesis support E17/A5. His systems account is an interpretation across selected technologies, not a universal quantitative model.
Invention, finance, organizations, production and cultural expectations support M15/U13/S12/F7. The focus on systems is more useful here than inventor anecdotes alone.
Broad cultural coverage lowers D7; the questions about large technical systems retain R9.
The structure is substantial but sometimes diffuse, N2/P2. It is explanatory history rather than engineering training. The national historical frame retains the thematic deduction.

books.sourceTitle: The Social Transformation of American Medicine
books.title: The Social Transformation of American Medicine
books.author: Paul Starr
books.eligibility: A sustained institutional history written for readers beyond medical training; not a medical textbook.
books.theme: -10: The history of the American medical system and profession predominates.
reason: Starr's scholarship and the book's specialist reception support E17/A5. Brandt's review identifies insufficient attention to scientific change and the patient-physician relationship, limiting the completeness of the causal account.

Professional authority, entry barriers, insurance and corporate organization support M15/U13/S11/F4. Those mechanisms transfer beyond medicine, but the book remains far from the preferred reading topics.
Long institutional history lowers D6; the mechanisms of professional power retain R9. The linked 2017 revision is not evidence that every fact is current in 2026.
The architecture is systematic and precise, N2/P2. The critique does not establish a serious central failure; American medical history receives the deduction.
books.editionNote: Linked paperback is the 2017 revised edition; 1982 is the first-publication year.

books.title: Prophets of Regulation
books.author: Thomas K. McCraw
books.eligibility: Four linked historical biographies and an argument about regulation, not a regulatory-compliance handbook.
books.theme: -10: American regulatory and political history predominates.
reason: Research-led biographies and McCraw's scholarly standing support E18/A5. Selection of influential individuals does not show that personalities alone determined regulation.
Industry structure, capture, agency design and changes in economic reasoning support M15/U13/S11/F5. These give the administrative detail a transferable purpose.
Four careers and their institutional settings lower D7; the questions of regulatory design retain R9.
The linked biographies form a readable argument, N3/P2. This is historical explanation, not compliance instruction. American regulatory and political history requires T=-10.

books.sourceTitle: Stalin, Vol. I: Paradoxes of Power, 1878–1928
books.title: Stalin, Vol. I: Paradoxes of Power, 1878–1928
books.author: Stephen Kotkin
books.eligibility: Historical biography for a broad readership; scholarship and length alone do not trigger rule 2.
books.theme: -10: A political ruler and Russian/Soviet national history predominate.
reason: Kotkin's archival scholarship supports E18/A5. Interpretation of ideology and individual agency still requires comparison with other histories.
State weakness, party organization, coercion and ideology support M13/U10/S11/F5. That is enough transferable content to avoid V3, without invoking the science-biography exception.
The large amount of biographical and national detail makes D4 appropriate for this reader. The historical subject retains R9.
The reconstruction is controlled and readable, N3/P2. The political subject is not itself ideological capture. The deduction and high reading cost make this a low personal priority.

books.title: Race for Profit
books.author: Keeanga-Yamahtta Taylor
books.eligibility: A public-facing archival history and argument about housing finance; no specialist methods course or procedural structure.
books.theme: -10: Racial history, American housing policy and urban history predominate.
reason: Archival research and scholarly reception support E17/A4. The documented policy setting supports a bounded historical claim, not a universal account of all housing markets.
Guarantees, intermediaries, poor incentives and failures of oversight support M14/U12/S10/F4. These are transferable mechanisms even though the dominant topic is unwanted.
The concentrated case history earns D7; its institutional lessons retain R8.
The argument is clear and controlled, N3/P2. Neither racial subject matter nor the author's politics establishes V2. The racial and urban focus receives one deduction.

books.title: Born in Flames
books.author: Bench Ansfield
books.eligibility: A narrative history of insurance, arson and housing, adapted for a general readership; dissertation origins do not decide eligibility.
books.theme: -10: American urban and racial history and local destruction predominate.
reason: Historical research and a substantive Housing Studies review support E16/A4. The causal scale of the insurance explanation has not been independently checked in the underlying archives here, so score confidence is low.
Divergence between insured and market value, landlord incentives, reinsurance and public policy support M14/U12/S10/F4. This is a genuine mechanism beyond names and neighborhoods.
The focused narrative earns D7; insurance incentives and moral hazard should remain useful, R8.
The investigation is coherent and readable, N3/P2. A recent publication about older institutions is not inherently ephemeral. American urban and racial history receives T=-10.
books.editionNote: Norton lists this paperback for 2 October 2026; 2025 is the first-publication year.

books.title: The First Tycoon
books.author: T. J. Stiles
books.eligibility: Historical business biography, not a management or investment manual.
books.theme: -10: American business biography and domestic institutional history dominate.
reason: Extensive historical research and Stiles's biographical standing support E18/A5. The achievement of one businessman is not a representative sample of all successful strategies.
Transport competition, consolidation, finance and corporate control support M14/U12/S11/F6. These give the biography substantial institutional content.
The long personal and commercial chronology lowers D5; the mechanisms and historical record retain R9.
The narrative is clear and the prose controlled, N3/P2. Transferable content defeats V3, but the predominant American biographical and institutional frame receives the deduction.

books.title: Plantation Goods
books.author: Seth Rockman
books.eligibility: A narrative material history connecting producers and users. The publisher's contents and general-reader reception support eligibility despite its specialist research base.
books.theme: -10: American slavery and racial history are the central subject.
reason: Archival material history supports E18/A4. Evidence of supply links is stronger than an unrestricted claim that those links explain all northern industrial development.
Product specifications, market dependence and supplier-customer relations support M13/U11/S11/F5. There is an economic mechanism beyond the objects' local stories.
Material detail and the historical argument support D7; the findings have enduring relevance, R8.

The cumulative structure is somewhat specialized but remains readable, N2/P2. General-reader purpose and a sustained narrative pass rule 2. The central slavery and racial-history subject receives T=-10.
books.editionNote: The publisher's BiblioVault record confirms the paperback ISBN, distinct from the 2024 cloth ISBN; 2024 is the first-publication year.

books.sourceTitle: The Soul of a New Machine
books.title: The Soul of a New Machine
books.author: Tracy Kidder
books.eligibility: Observed narrative of one engineering project, not computer-design training.
books.theme: 0: A technical team's work and engineering organization; not a national or urban history and not an American-tragedy narrative.
reason: Close observation of engineers at work and an established reporting achievement support E18/A5. One team and one project still limit causal generalization.
Deadlines, design compromises, tacit knowledge and team incentives support M14/U13/S10/F7. These mechanisms survive the specific hardware.
The focused account earns D8; organizational lessons retain R9 despite obsolete computer details.
The project narrative and exact prose support N3/P2. It teaches through observation rather than technical exercises. The prior 89 and all components remain supported.

books.title: The Heavens and the Earth
books.author: Walter A. McDougall
books.eligibility: Comparative historical explanation of space policy; technical and administrative detail serves the historical argument.
books.theme: 0: Explicitly comparative US, Soviet and European space policy, with international influence.
reason: Archival, interview and comparative historical work support E18/A5. The book must be read with its original access limits, especially for the Soviet side, rather than as a complete current space-policy account.
Military competition, public finance, research institutions and state capacity support M15/U13/S12/F7. Its comparison of political systems supplies strong strategic value.
Detailed policy history reduces D6; the relationships between state capacity and technical ambition retain R9.
The analytical structure is demanding but controlled, N2/P2. The explicitly comparative scope avoids the single-nation deduction; it is not a procedural policy handbook.
books.editionNote: The 1997 Johns Hopkins paperback is linked. The original work was published in 1985, confirmed by WorldCat; a Goodreads import's 2013 date is not the first-publication year.

books.title: The Box
books.author: Marc Levinson
books.eligibility: Narrative economic history of container adoption, not a logistics manual.
books.theme: 0: Global transport systems and trade. Port-city changes are effects within that global system.
reason: Research into the adoption process supports E18/A4. The strongest evidence concerns the historical sequence; assigning all globalization gains to containerization would go beyond it.
Standards, complementary investment, labor arrangements and transport costs support M16/U14/S12/F7. The book explains why a simple device required coordinated system change.
The cases largely advance that explanation, D8, and the mechanisms remain durable, R9.
The narrative is clear and disciplined, N3/P2. The linked second edition adds a chapter, while 2006 remains the work's first-publication year. No technical-manual exclusion applies.
books.editionNote: Linked paperback is the 2016 second edition with an added chapter; 2006 is the first-publication year.

books.title: The Alchemy of Air
books.author: Thomas Hager
books.eligibility: Science and industrial history told through Haber and Bosch; not chemistry instruction.
books.theme: 0: Industrial chemistry, food production and war-making capability; environmental effects are not the predominant account.
reason: Science reporting and biographical research support E17/A4. Dramatic framing must not turn Haber-Bosch into a single sufficient cause of later wars or population change.
Catalysis, industrial scale-up, capital, agriculture and military supply support M14/U13/S12/F7. The strength is the bridge from laboratory discovery to production.
The relatively compact account earns D9; the technological and institutional mechanisms retain R8.
The paired lives provide clear narrative structure, N3/P2. It is industrial-science history for general readers, not a chemistry textbook or predominantly an environmental account.

books.title: The Wages of Destruction
books.author: Adam Tooze
books.eligibility: A sustained economic history for readers outside specialist training; quantitative evidence supports a narrative argument.
books.theme: -10: Nazi Germany's national economic history remains the main subject despite international constraints and consequences.
reason: Quantitative economic history and specialist engagement support E18/A5. Richard Evans's assessment supports the work's standing; the Historical Materialism critique shows that the bridge from economic structure to aggression remains contested.

Foreign-exchange limits, resource constraints, industrial capacity and strategic choices support M16/U14/S12/F7. The model is useful without making economic scarcity a sufficient explanation of Nazi policy.
Extensive detail lowers D6; the account of constraints and mobilization retains R9.

The argument is demanding but conceptually controlled, N2/P2. Neither a hostile regime as subject nor disagreement between historians proves V2 or V1. Germany-centered economic history receives T=-10.

books.title: The World for Sale
books.author: Javier Blas; Jack Farchy
books.eligibility: Investigative narrative of commodity trading and political power, not a trading handbook.
books.theme: 0: Worldwide commodity trade, credit, logistics and geopolitics.
reason: Industry reporting and access support E17/A4. Private-company records and trader interviews provide unusual evidence, but access can leave selection and self-presentation biases.
Credit, logistics, information asymmetry and political brokerage support M15/U14/S12/F7. These connect physical resources to financial and state power.
The reported cases are concentrated enough for D8; changing firms and transactions limit R to 8 while the intermediary mechanisms endure.
The narrative is readable and controlled, N3/P2. Its value does not depend on a passing commodity-price episode, and it offers explanation rather than trading instructions.

books.title: Energy and Civilization
books.author: Vaclav Smil
books.eligibility: A chronological explanatory history of energy and civilization. Quantities and diagrams support synthesis, rather than exercises or specialist instruction.
books.theme: 0: Energy conversion and economic history are central; energy is not automatically an environmental topic.
reason: Quantitative synthesis and Smil's domain expertise support E18/A5. Historical estimates have unequal quality, and energy accounting should not be confused with a complete causal theory of institutions.
Energy conversion, power density, labor, production and transport support M16/U14/S12/F7. Physical constraints make it especially useful for this reader.
Many quantities and examples demand effort and reduce D7, while the underlying constraints retain R9.
The chronological synthesis is dense but precise, N2/P2. Equations and figures do not make it a training text. The predominant topic is civilization's material operation, not environmental advocacy.

books.title: The Pursuit of Power
books.author: William H. McNeill
books.eligibility: Comparative historical synthesis of technology, armed force and society; not a military field manual.
books.theme: 0: Comparative military, technological and economic history across societies.
reason: McNeill's scholarship and broad synthesis support E17/A5. Its scale and age limit detailed causal discrimination and require care with later research.
Military competition, commercialization, state finance and technological change support M16/U14/S12/F7. The feedback between armed force and production is strongly transferable.
The broad historical narrative lowers D7; the mechanisms retain R9. Its terminal Cold War context is historical, not a present-day strategic forecast.
The architecture is demanding but controlled, N2/P2. The comparison across societies avoids a single-nation deduction and supplies ample content under V3.

books.title: Seeing Like a State
books.author: James C. Scott
books.eligibility: A sustained comparative argument about state simplification and local knowledge, not administrative instruction.
books.theme: 0: Comparative state knowledge and planning; urban and environmental cases do not exhaust its subject.
reason: Comparative scholarship supports E16/A5. Selection of failed schemes constrains inference about the average success of all state planning.
Legibility, simplified metrics and lost local knowledge support M16/U14/S11/F6. These mechanisms transfer to models, organizations and engineering design.
Some repeated case framing keeps D7; the information and coordination problems retain R9.

The narrative cases and disciplined concepts support N3/P2. The argument need not be read as a universal anti-state claim. The prior full vector remains justified; reader enthusiasm adds no causal evidence.

books.title: The Gunpowder Age
books.author: Tonio Andrade
books.eligibility: Comparative narrative history of military innovation, not artillery or military-technical training.
books.theme: 0: Comparison of Chinese and European military development, not a single-nation history.
reason: Historical research and specialist engagement support E18/A4. The comparative thesis remains an explanation to assess, not a settled single cause of global divergence.
Military competition, learning, adoption and periods of reduced pressure support M15/U13/S12/F7. Technology is linked to institutions and strategic context.
Campaign and weapon detail lowers D7; the mechanisms retain R8, with room for revision of the comparative history.
The chronology is clear and the distinctions controlled, N3/P2. The China-Europe comparison is central, so the presence of China in the subtitle does not trigger a national-history deduction.

books.title: The Shock of the Old
books.author: David Edgerton
books.eligibility: A sustained historical argument about technology in use, not a technical reference or invention manual.
books.theme: 0: Global technological use, maintenance and diffusion.
reason: Historical scholarship supports E17/A4. Selected counterexamples expose a bias toward invention dates but do not measure the importance of every technology.
Use, maintenance, adaptation and diffusion support M14/U15/S11/F7. Distinguishing novelty from practical contribution is a highly reusable heuristic.
The focused corrective earns D8; its resistance to novelty-driven thinking supports R9.
The thematic chapters can be less cumulative than a single narrative, N2, while conceptual discipline supports P2. It is durable argument, not a buzzword-dependent account.

books.title: Most Secret War
books.author: R. V. Jones
books.eligibility: A physicist's scientific-intelligence memoir; it describes reasoning in context rather than teaching an operational procedure.
books.theme: 0: Scientific intelligence in an international war; a British viewpoint alone does not make this a national-history narrative.
reason: First-hand scientific expertise supports E16/A4, with the limits of retrospective memory and an insider's account of his own role.
Evidence fusion, deception, testing rival explanations and countermeasure cycles support M15/U14/S11/F7. They offer concrete reasoning lessons for a physicist.
Wartime episodes and personal detail keep D7. The epistemic and organizational lessons retain R9.

The memoir is clear and controlled, N3/P2. It qualifies under the scientific-memoir exception as well as possessing transferable content; operational obsolescence does not remove its historical value.

books.title: Countdown to Zero Day
books.author: Kim Zetter
books.eligibility: Investigative history of Stuxnet's discovery and use, not exploit development or malware-operation instruction.
books.theme: 0: A cross-border technological operation and strategic risk; neither Iran nor the US supplies an isolated national history.
reason: Technical reporting and reconstruction of the investigation support E17/A4. Attribution and state intentions contain more uncertainty than the visible technical evidence.
Detection, inference from artifacts, industrial-system dependencies and strategic escalation support M15/U14/S11/F7. These fit computing and technological risk closely.
The focused investigation earns D8; individual vulnerabilities age, but the broader failure modes retain R8.

The discovery narrative is strong, N3. P1 discounts headline-level certainty, including the expansive 'first digital weapon' framing. No central failure sufficient for V1 is established; this is not a malware manual.

books.title: How Asia Works
books.author: Joe Studwell
books.eligibility: A comparative argument about development policies, not an economics textbook despite its practical conclusions.
books.theme: 0: Comparative industrial development across Asian economies.
reason: Regional reporting and comparative cases support E15/A4. Policy selection, omitted conditions and counterfactual uncertainty prevent treating the preferred policy sequence as a proven universal recipe.
Land reform, export discipline, industrial learning and financial allocation support M15/U14/S12/F6. The mechanisms are strategically useful even when policy transfer is uncertain.
Some repetition and long cases keep D7; the structural questions retain R8.
The argument is clear and disciplined, N3/P2. A position favoring industrial policy is not itself ideological capture; the observed evidence does not establish a serious V2 veto.

books.title: The Idea Factory
books.author: Jon Gertner
books.eligibility: Institutional history of Bell Labs and its inventions, not technical training.
books.theme: 0: A research institution and globally consequential inventions; its US location alone does not make it national history.
reason: Reported institutional history supports E17/A3. The evidence is strongest for the particular laboratory; retrospective selection of famous successes limits the general explanation of innovation.
Long funding horizons, production links, interactions among researchers and organizational freedom support M15/U14/S11/F7. These are relevant to scientific organization.
The focused institutional narrative earns D8, and the research-management questions retain R9.
Linked biographies and inventions provide a clear structure, N3/P2. Bell Labs' US location does not make the book predominantly American civil history; the technical influence is international.

books.title: Power and Plenty
books.author: Ronald Findlay; Kevin H. O’Rourke
books.eligibility: The preface explicitly addresses economists and general readers; chronological world-trade chapters form a sustained explanation. Its use as a reference or on courses does not change that main purpose.
books.theme: 0: World trade, warfare and growth across regions.
reason: Scholarly synthesis, economic evidence and specialist reception support E18/A5. Sparse early trade data and reliance on varied secondary histories prevent maximum evidential confidence.
Trade costs, coercion, state power and regional specialization support M16/U14/S12/F7. Feedback runs both ways between commerce and military capacity.
The long history is dense but mostly purposeful, D7; its comparative mechanisms retain R9.

The chronological structure is demanding, N2, and the concepts are controlled, P2. The preface and contents establish an explanatory account for general readers, so 'reference-grade' praise does not trigger rule 2.
